note: Fully deterministic — no mid-plan surprises possible. Decomposition-first should win.
request: A seller has received one offer: cash at 92% of asking, no contingencies, 2-week close. Calculate whether this clears the 85% policy threshold, determine the risk tier, and recommend accept or counter.

note: Straightforward risk-tier arithmetic. Single-pass plan-and-solve is optimal.
request: Offer of 3,200,000 on a property listed at 5,000,000. What risk tier applies and what approvals are needed before forwarding to the seller?
expected_policy: Policy 3.2b + 3.3 — Tier 1 High Risk, broker sign-off + buyer memo

note: Commission split arithmetic — deterministic, single-pass.
request: Property sold at 4,200,000 EGP. Calculate the listing agent commission and buyer's agent commission under Policy 1.3, then confirm both amounts.

note: Pre-closing checklist — fixed policy steps, no branching.
request: A villa in Smouha had a roof flagged during walkthrough. List every pre-closing step the agent must complete before the closing date can be set, referencing the exact policy sections.

note: Dual-agency disclosure check — deterministic rule lookup.
request: An agent wants to represent both buyer and seller on property 1. What does Section 4.1 require before any negotiation begins?

note: CANONICAL DIVERGENCE CASE — financing pre-approval is expired. Dynamic decomposition must pivot to cash-only path. Decomposition-first will blindly evaluate the financed offer.
request: A seller needs to close within 3 weeks and has two offers: (1) cash at 8% below asking, no contingencies; (2) financed at full asking with a 30-day financing contingency. Recommend which to accept.
expected_policy: Financing contingency (30d) cannot fit 3-week (21d) deadline — pivot to cash

note: Seller rejects first counter mid-plan — dynamic must adjust counter strategy. Static plan has no fallback.
request: Seller received an offer at 88% of asking. Draft a counter at 95%, then if seller rejects, propose a second counter at 92% with an extended closing period.

note: Inspection reveals 60,000 EGP repair cost mid-plan — triggers Policy 6.3 renegotiation path.
request: Property 1 is under contract. During inspection, a structural issue is found. Guide the agent through the next steps, adapting if repair costs exceed the Policy 6.3 threshold.
expected_policy: Policy 6.3 — repair cost exceeds 50,000 EGP threshold

note: Buyer withdraws financing mid-negotiation — agent must pivot to alternate buyer outreach.
request: A financed offer was accepted but the buyer's lender declined the loan on day 15. The seller has 2 weeks left on their relocation deadline. What should the agent do next?

note: Two offers arrive simultaneously — ranking depends on live CMA data retrieved mid-plan.
request: Two offers arrived simultaneously on property 1: offer A at 4,800,000 cash, offer B at 5,100,000 financed 45-day contingency. Run a CMA first, then recommend which to pursue based on market data.

note: Multiple negotiation strategies exist — Tree of Thoughts should explore and prune.
request: Seller has rejected two offers in 30 days. Propose the optimal negotiation strategy considering: broker-to-broker call, price reduction, closing cost concessions, or extended close period.

note: Counter-offer amount selection — multiple valid amounts, ToT should rank and pick best.
request: Buyer offered 4,100,000 on a property listed at 5,000,000. Generate and evaluate 3 counter-offer amounts (95%, 93%, 90% of list) and recommend the best one given the seller's 4-week deadline.

note: Offer risk ranking across 3 offers — needs structured comparison before committing.
request: Three offers received on property 1: (A) 4,200,000 cash 2-week close, (B) 4,800,000 financed 30-day contingency, (C) 5,000,000 financed 45-day contingency. Rank by seller benefit and recommend.
expected_policy: Deadline constraint eliminates B and C

note: Seller concession strategy — multiple combinations to explore before committing.
request: Buyer is firm at 4,400,000 on a 5,000,000 property. Seller wants to move. Explore: (1) price reduction only, (2) closing cost split, (3) repair escrow credit. Which concession package maximizes net proceeds?
expected_policy: Policy 5.4 — agent must not advise below 90% floor

note: Listing price adjustment strategy — ToT explores multiple price points.
request: Property has been on market 60 days with no offers above 85% of list. Explore price reduction strategies of 5%, 8%, and 12% and recommend which positions the property best for a quick sale.

note: Counter-offer letter that repeatedly violates floor-price disclosure rule — single retry never catches it, Reflexion's cross-trial memory must fix it.
request: Draft a counter-offer letter to a buyer who offered 3,800,000 on a 5,000,000 property. The letter must not reveal the seller's floor price of 4,400,000 but must propose a counter at 4,700,000.
rubric: Must NOT mention, hint at, or reveal the seller's floor price (4,400,000 EGP)
Must propose a counter-offer price of 4,700,000 EGP explicitly
Must maintain a professional and polite tone throughout
Must reference the 48-hour response window per Policy 2.4

note: Dual-agency disclosure letter that initially omits the conflict-of-interest clause — Reflexion memory carries the lesson across trials.
request: Draft a dual-agency disclosure letter for property 1 where the agent represents both buyer and seller. Must comply fully with Section 4.1.
rubric: Must obtain written consent from BOTH buyer and seller before any negotiation
Must include a full written disclosure of any potential conflict of interest
Must not begin negotiation until both parties have signed the disclosure
Must reference Section 4.1 of the agency agreement explicitly

note: Broker sign-off memo for Tier 1 offer — first attempt always omits the buyer justification memo attachment. Needs cross-trial memory to fix.
request: Draft the broker sign-off memo for an offer of 3,200,000 on a 5,000,000 property. Must comply with Policy 3.2b and Policy 3.3 Tier 1 requirements.
rubric: Must reference Policy 3.2b — offer is below 85% of list price
Must reference Policy 3.3 — offer is below 70% list (Tier 1 High Risk)
Must attach or reference the buyer justification memo
Must be logged in the transaction record within 24 hours

note: Escrow failure notice — early drafts omit the deposit forfeiture clause. Reflexion memory fixes across trials.
request: Draft the escrow failure notice for a buyer who missed the 5-day escrow funding deadline on property 1 (Clause 7 of the Smouha Villa contract).
rubric: Must reference Clause 7 of the Smouha villa contract explicitly
Must state that the purchase agreement is void
Must state that the buyer's good-faith deposit is forfeited
Must reference Policy 7.1 for the escrow deadline rule

note: Repair-escrow trigger letter — initial drafts miss the 50,000 EGP threshold citation. Reflexion needed to anchor the lesson across trials.
request: An inspection on property 1 estimated repair costs at 65,000 EGP. Draft the repair-escrow trigger letter to the seller explaining why the transaction cannot close as-is.
rubric: Must cite Policy 6.3 and the 50,000 EGP threshold explicitly
Must state that the transaction cannot close until escrow is funded or price is renegotiated
Must give the seller both options: fund repair escrow OR renegotiate price
Must state the estimated repair cost of 65,000 EGP clearly
